source.anchor: Original Samplinglib supplement: One almost-everywhere subsequence for countably many limits in measure. Exact assumptions and formula below.
source.original_text:
Suppose a countable family of sequences into a pseudo extended metric space each converges in measure. A single strictly increasing subsequence makes every sequence in the family converge to its stated limit almost everywhere on the same event.

The family index type is countable and the sample space carries a measure. The codomain is a pseudo extended metric space.
For each family member, its sequence converges in measure to the specified limit, defined through the measure of each positive extended-distance error event.

\exists\,k:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N\ \text{strictly increasing},\qquad \mu\text{-a.e. } \omega,\ \forall i,\quad F_{i,k(n)}(\omega)\to G_i(\omega).

blind_reconstruction.text:
Countable type I; measurable Omega with arbitrary measure mu; pseudo-extended-metric space E; sequences F_i,n and target functions G_i; common subsequence k.

F:I→N→Omega→E; G:I→Omega→E; k:N→N. E has PseudoEMetricSpace structure. No measure finiteness or separate measurability hypotheses are stated.

Assumptions: I countable; each individual sequence converges in measure under the same mu.

Conclusion: There is one strictly increasing subsequence k common to all i and one mu-full set on which all the pointwise sequences converge in the topology of E to their respective G_i values.

Quantifier order: Assume for every i∈I, F_i,n tends to G_i in mu-measure as n→infinity. Then there exists k:N→N, strictly increasing, such that for mu-a.e. omega, simultaneously for every i∈I, F_i,k(n)(omega)→G_i(omega).

Scope: Order is exists k, then mu-almost every omega, then every i, then n→infinity. No uniform convergence in i or omega is asserted; mu is arbitrary.

Constant dependencies: k may depend on the whole family F,G,I,mu and E, and is independent of i and omega.

import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.ConvergenceInMeasure
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.BorelCantelli

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.CountableConvergenceInMeasure

open Filter MeasureTheory Set
open scoped ENNReal Topology

/-- A countable family of limits in measure has a common almost-everywhere subsequence. -/
theorem exists_seq_tendsto_ae_of_countable
    {I Ω E : Type*} [Countable I] [MeasurableSpace Ω] [PseudoEMetricSpace E]
    {μ : Measure Ω} {F : I → ℕ → Ω → E} {G : I → Ω → E}
    (h : ∀ i, TendstoInMeasure μ (F i) atTop (G i)) :
    ∃ k : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono k ∧ ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, ∀ i,
      Tendsto (fun n => F i (k n) ω) atTop (𝓝 (G i ω)) := by
  let _ : Encodable I := Encodable.ofCountable I
  let pick (j n : ℕ) := ((Encodable.decode j : Option I).map
    (fun i => ExistsSeqTendstoAe.seqTendstoAeSeq (h i) n)).getD 0
  let bound (n : ℕ) := (Finset.range (n + 1)).sup (fun j => pick j n)
  let k (n : ℕ) := n + bound n
  have hPick (j : ℕ) : Monotone (pick j) := by
    intro m n hmn
    cases hj : (Encodable.decode j : Option I) with
    | none => simp [pick, hj]
    | some i =>
      simpa [pick, hj] using (ExistsSeqTendstoAe.seqTendstoAeSeq_strictMono (h i)).monotone hmn
  have hBound : Monotone bound := by
    intro m n hmn
    apply Finset.sup_le_iff.2
    intro j hj
    exact (hPick j hmn).trans
      (Finset.le_sup (f := fun j => pick j n) (Finset.range_mono (Nat.succ_le_succ hmn) hj))
  have hk : StrictMono k := fun _ _ hmn => Nat.add_lt_add_of_lt_of_le hmn (hBound hmn.le)
  refine ⟨k, hk, ae_all_iff.2 ?_⟩
  intro i
  let S (n : ℕ) : Set Ω := if Encodable.encode i ≤ n then
    {ω | (2 : ℝ≥0∞)⁻¹ ^ n ≤ edist (F i (k n) ω) (G i ω)} else ∅
  have hMeasure (n : ℕ) : μ (S n) ≤ (2 : ℝ≥0∞)⁻¹ ^ n := by
    by_cases hn : Encodable.encode i ≤ n
    · have hp : pick (Encodable.encode i) n ≤ bound n :=
        Finset.le_sup (f := fun j => pick j n) (Finset.mem_range.2 (Nat.lt_succ_of_le hn))
      have hIndex : ExistsSeqTendstoAe.seqTendstoAeSeq (h i) n ≤ k n :=
        (by simpa [pick] using hp : _ ≤ bound n).trans (Nat.le_add_left _ _)
      simpa [S, hn] using ExistsSeqTendstoAe.seqTendstoAeSeq_spec (h i) n (k n) hIndex
    · simp [S, hn]
  have hFinite : (∑' n, μ (S n)) ≠ ∞ := by
    refine ne_top_of_le_ne_top ?_ (ENNReal.tsum_le_tsum hMeasure)
    simpa only [ENNReal.tsum_geometric, ENNReal.one_sub_inv_two, inv_inv] using ENNReal.ofNat_ne_top
  filter_upwards [ae_eventually_notMem hFinite] with ω hω
  refine EMetric.tendsto_atTop.mpr fun ε hε => eventually_atTop.1 ?_
  have hSmall : ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (2 : ℝ≥0∞)⁻¹ ^ n < ε :=
    (ENNReal.tendsto_pow_atTop_nhds_zero_of_lt_one (by norm_num)).eventually_lt_const hε
  filter_upwards [hω, hSmall, eventually_ge_atTop (Encodable.encode i)] with n hn hs hi
  have hErr : edist (F i (k n) ω) (G i ω) < (2 : ℝ≥0∞)⁻¹ ^ n := by
    simpa [S, hi] using hn
  exact hErr.trans hs

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.CountableConvergenceInMeasure

steps.title: Choose one index for each tolerance
steps.text: Encode the countable family into natural numbers. For each sequence, the usual geometric error thresholds can be chosen nondecreasing in n. The maximum over codes at most n is then nondecreasing as both the thresholds and the set of codes grow. Adding n makes the selected indices strictly increasing.

lesson.lean_statement: The theorem uses an arbitrary measure and the same samplewise event for all countably many limits.
lesson.lean_proof: Use a monotone finite maximum of Mathlib's geometric thresholds, apply Borel–Cantelli separately to each member, then take a countable intersection.
